Reliance on this Executive Summary alone, without review of the full report, may result in an incomplete understanding of the environmental conditions associated with the Subject Property.
125	
126	**[Section 1: Purpose and Scope]{.underline}**
127	
128	This Executive Summary presents the findings of a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase I ESA\") conducted in accordance with ASTM E1527-21, *Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessments: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment Process*, for the property known as Meridian Corporate Center, located at 11600, 11620, and 11640 Corporate Park Drive, Reston, Virginia 20191 (the \"Subject Property\" or \"Property\").
129	
130	The assessment was commissioned by Calverley Capital Partners LLC (the \"Client\") in connection with a proposed acquisition of the Property from Meridian Office Holdings LP (the \"Seller\"). The purpose of this Phase I ESA is to identify Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"RECs\"), Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"CRECs\"), and Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"HRECs\") in connection with the Subject Property, as those terms are defined under ASTM E1527-21.
131	
132	This assessment is intended to satisfy the \"All Appropriate Inquiries\" (\"AAI\") standard codified at 40 CFR Part 312, promulgated by the United States Environmental Protection Agency pursuant to the Small Business Liability Relief and Brownfields Revitalization Act of 2002. Compliance with the AAI standard qualifies the Client for certain liability protections available under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (\"CERCLA\"), 42 U.S.C. §§ 9601 *et seq.*, including the \"innocent landowner,\" \"contiguous property owner,\" and \"bona fide prospective purchaser\" defenses.
133	
134	The scope of this Phase I ESA includes: (i) a review of federal, state, tribal, and local regulatory agency records and databases; (ii) a review of historical sources, including aerial photographs, Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps, topographic maps, building permits, land records, and city directories; (iii) a site reconnaissance of the Subject Property and visual observation of adjoining properties; (iv) interviews with knowledgeable parties regarding the environmental history and condition of the Subject Property; and (v) evaluation of the Subject Property and adjoining properties for evidence of potential environmental conditions.
135	
136	Site reconnaissance was conducted on July 29--30, 2024, by Dr. Karen M. Whitfield, P.G., Senior Environmental Scientist with Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC. Interviews were conducted with Marcus Ellison, President of Meridian GP Inc. (the general partner of the Seller), and members of the on-site property management team retained by the Seller.
137	
138	This document is an Executive Summary. The full Phase I ESA report contains detailed findings, methodology descriptions, appendices, regulatory database search results, historical documentation, site photographs, and the complete limiting conditions and qualifications applicable to this assessment.
139	
140	**[Section 2: Property Description]{.underline}**
141	
142	**Property Name:** Meridian Corporate Center
143	
144	**Addresses:** 11600 Corporate Park Drive (Building A), 11620 Corporate Park Drive (Building B), and 11640 Corporate Park Drive (Building C), Reston, Virginia 20191, Fairfax County, Virginia
145	
146	**Tax Map Parcels:** 0264-01-0017A, 0264-01-0017B, and 0264-01-0017C (Fairfax County)
147	
148	**Total Acreage:** Approximately 22.8 acres
149	
150	**Improvements:** The Subject Property is improved with three Class A suburban office buildings constructed in 2013, totaling approximately 312,000 rentable square feet. Building A (11600 Corporate Park Drive) contains approximately 118,000 rentable square feet. Building B (11620 Corporate Park Drive) contains approximately 104,000 rentable square feet. Building C (11640 Corporate Park Drive) contains approximately 90,000 rentable square feet. The buildings are steel-frame, glass-curtain-wall construction, each ranging from four to five stories in height.
151	
152	**Structured Parking Garage:** The Subject Property includes a structured parking garage containing approximately 1,248 parking spaces, providing a parking ratio of approximately 4.0 spaces per 1,000 rentable square feet of office space.
153	
154	**Current Occupancy:** The Subject Property is approximately 82% occupied by 14 commercial tenants. Tenant uses consist primarily of professional office, professional services, technology, and government contractor operations. No industrial, manufacturing, laboratory, or chemical-intensive tenant uses were identified.
155	
156	**Site Topography:** The Subject Property exhibits generally flat to gently sloping terrain. Surface drainage is directed toward the southwest, consistent with the area\'s natural topographic gradient. The southwest portion of the site, in the vicinity of Building C, is at a slightly lower elevation than the northeast portion of the site where Building A is located. Elevation across the site ranges from approximately 340 feet above mean sea level (northeast) to approximately 325 feet above mean sea level (southwest).
157	
158	**Utilities:** The Subject Property is served by public water (Fairfax Water) and public sewer (Fairfax County Wastewater Management Program). No private water supply wells or on-site septic systems were identified during the assessment.
159	
160	**Prior Use of Subject Property:** Prior to 2011, the Subject Property consisted of undeveloped land zoned for planned development within the Reston community. Site grading and construction activities commenced in 2012, and building construction was substantially completed in 2013. Based on the historical sources reviewed, no prior commercial, industrial, agricultural, or other potentially contaminating use of the Subject Property was identified during any period of record.
161	
162	**Current Owner:** Meridian Office Holdings LP, a Virginia limited partnership formed on September 22, 2011. Meridian Office Holdings LP developed the Subject Property and has continuously held fee simple ownership of the Property since construction. The general partner of Meridian Office Holdings LP is Meridian GP Inc., a Virginia corporation.
163	
164	**[Section 3: Historical Use Review]{.underline}**
165	
166	**Methodology.** The historical use review was conducted in accordance with the requirements of ASTM E1527-21, Section 8.3. Historical sources reviewed include: Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps (where available for the Subject Property and surrounding area); historical aerial photographs dated 1957, 1971, 1983, 1994, 2002, 2010, 2015, and 2020; historical topographic maps from the United States Geological Survey (USGS) 7.5-minute quadrangle series; Fairfax County building permits and land records; and historical city directories for the Reston, Virginia area.
167	
168	**Subject Property History**
169	
170	Review of historical aerial photographs from 1957 through 2002 consistently depicts the Subject Property as undeveloped woodland and scrubland, with no structures, cleared areas, or evidence of any commercial, industrial, or agricultural use visible in any photograph during this period. No Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps were available for the Subject Property itself, as the Property was located outside of the historically mapped areas until the expansion of suburban development in western Fairfax County in recent decades.
171	
172	The 2010 aerial photograph shows active grading and site preparation on the Subject Property, consistent with the commencement of construction activities in 2012. The 2015 aerial photograph depicts the three office buildings and the structured parking garage, consistent with the 2013 construction completion date confirmed by Fairfax County certificate of occupancy records.
173	
174	No evidence of underground storage tanks (USTs), above-ground storage tanks (ASTs), dry cleaning operations, gasoline service stations, manufacturing facilities, chemical storage, landfilling, or other potentially contaminating uses on the Subject Property was identified through the historical record review.
175	
176	**Adjoining Properties --- Critical Finding**
177	
178	The parcel immediately to the southwest of the Subject Property (Fairfax County Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019, an approximately 3.2-acre parcel currently improved with a retail strip center constructed circa 2006) formerly housed a commercial dry cleaning facility.
179	
180	Sanborn Fire Insurance Maps (1988 edition) and historical city directories for the Reston, Virginia area confirm that a commercial dry cleaning business operating under the name \"Reston Village Cleaners\" occupied a freestanding commercial building at the approximate location of the current retail strip center from approximately 1985 to 2003. The dry cleaning operation utilized tetrachloroethylene (also known as perchloroethylene, or \"PCE\") as its primary dry cleaning solvent, as confirmed by Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (\"DEQ\") records and historical business permit filings with Fairfax County.
181	
182	The former dry cleaning building was demolished in approximately 2004--2005 in connection with redevelopment of the adjacent parcel. The existing retail strip center was constructed in 2006 by an unrelated developer.
183	
184	Virginia DEQ records indicate that a Voluntary Remediation Program (\"VRP\") case (VRP File No. VRP-00487) was opened for the adjacent parcel in 2004 in connection with the planned redevelopment. DEQ records indicate that soil sampling conducted during the VRP investigation process in 2004 identified PCE concentrations in soil at levels exceeding the Virginia Voluntary Remediation Program Tier II screening levels applicable at that time. Limited soil remediation, consisting of excavation and off-site disposal of approximately 200 cubic yards of PCE-impacted soil, was conducted in 2005. The Virginia DEQ issued a Certificate of Satisfactory Completion of Remediation in March 2006 for the adjacent parcel only.
185	
186	However, the DEQ VRP file indicates that groundwater sampling conducted during the 2004--2005 investigation detected PCE in groundwater at concentrations up to 87 micrograms per liter (µg/L) in a monitoring well located on the southern boundary of the adjacent parcel. The applicable Virginia Groundwater Quality Standard for PCE is 5 µg/L, meaning the detected concentration exceeded the applicable standard by a factor of approximately 17.4. The VRP closure letter issued by DEQ in March 2006 included the following notation: \"groundwater impacts associated with the former dry cleaning operation may extend beyond the boundaries of the Property\" and that \"further investigation of potential off-site migration may be warranted.\" The closure letter did not require further action by the VRP applicant with respect to potential off-site contamination.
187	
188	Regional groundwater flow direction in the vicinity of the Subject Property, based on USGS hydrogeologic data and Fairfax County hydrogeologic mapping, is generally from the northeast to the southwest. However, localized groundwater flow patterns in the immediate area may be influenced by the structured parking garage foundation, building foundations, and stormwater management features constructed on the Subject Property, potentially creating a more complex groundwater flow regime than the regional pattern would suggest. The Subject Property --- specifically the southwest corner of the site where Building C (11640 Corporate Park Drive) is located --- is cross-gradient to slightly downgradient from the location of the former dry cleaning facility on the adjacent parcel.
189	
190	**Other Adjoining Properties**
191	
192	No other adjoining properties were identified with environmental conditions of concern. Properties to the north and east of the Subject Property consist of commercial office developments of similar vintage to the Subject Property. The property to the west of the Subject Property is a Fairfax County parkland parcel with no identified prior commercial, industrial, or other potentially contaminating use.
193	
194	**[Section 4: Regulatory Database Review]{.underline}**
195	
196	**Methodology.** A standard ASTM E1527-21 environmental regulatory database search was conducted by Environmental DataLink Services Inc. on July 15, 2024. The database search covered applicable federal, state, tribal, and local regulatory databases within the search radii specified by ASTM E1527-21, including but not limited to the EPA National Priorities List (NPL), CERCLIS/SEMS, RCRA CORRACTS, RCRA TSD, RCRA SQG/LQG, ERNS, Virginia DEQ Solid Waste facilities, Virginia DEQ Underground Storage Tank (UST) database, Virginia DEQ Voluntary Remediation Program (VRP) database, Virginia DEQ Petroleum Release database, and Fairfax County environmental records.
197	
198	**Subject Property.** The Subject Property (Tax Map Parcels 0264-01-0017A, 0264-01-0017B, and 0264-01-0017C) is not listed in any federal, state, or local environmental regulatory database searched as part of this assessment. No enforcement actions, violations, spills, releases, or remediation activities associated with the Subject Property were identified.
199	
200	**Adjacent Parcel (Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019).** The parcel immediately to the southwest of the Subject Property is listed in the following databases:
201	
202	> • **Virginia DEQ Voluntary Remediation Program (VRP) Database** --- VRP File No. VRP-00487. Case status: Closed. Certificate of Satisfactory Completion of Remediation issued March 2006. The VRP closure addressed the adjacent parcel only and, as discussed in Section 3 above, included an explicit notation that groundwater impacts may extend beyond the boundaries of that parcel.
203	>
204	> • **Virginia DEQ Underground Storage Tank (UST) Database** --- One 500-gallon heating oil underground storage tank was removed from the former dry cleaning facility site in 2004 during redevelopment activities. The UST closure letter issued by DEQ indicated that no petroleum release was detected in connection with the tank removal, and no further action was required with respect to the UST.
205	
206	**Other Nearby Facilities.** One facility located at 11580 Corporate Park Drive, approximately 0.3 miles to the northeast of the Subject Property, is listed as a RCRA Small Quantity Generator (SQG). The facility is identified as a commercial printing operation. No violations, releases, or corrective action requirements are associated with this listing. This facility is outside the ASTM-specified search radius for concern relative to the Subject Property and is not considered to represent a potential environmental concern.
207	
208	No other facilities within applicable ASTM search radii were identified as posing a potential environmental concern to the Subject Property.
209	
210	The regulatory database findings corroborate the historical use review findings discussed in Section 3 and confirm that while the adjacent parcel was remediated and closed under the VRP program, the closure was explicitly limited to the adjacent parcel and did not address the potential for off-site groundwater migration of PCE toward the Subject Property.
211	
212	**[Section 5: Site Reconnaissance Observations]{.underline}**
213	
214	**Date of Site Visit:** July 29--30, 2024
215	
216	**Conducted by:** Dr. Karen M. Whitfield, P.G., Senior Environmental Scientist, Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC
217	
218	**General Observations.** The three office buildings and the structured parking garage are in good overall condition, consistent with their 2013 construction date. Building systems, including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), plumbing, fire suppression, and electrical systems, appeared to be well-maintained based on visual observation and review of available maintenance records. No evidence of hazardous materials storage, underground storage tanks, above-ground storage tanks, drums, or chemical containers (other than de minimis quantities of building maintenance supplies as noted in Section 6.4) was observed on the Subject Property.
219	
220	**Specific Observations. Asbestos-Containing Materials (ACM).** Given the 2013 construction date, the buildings are unlikely to contain asbestos-containing materials. No suspect ACM was observed during the site reconnaissance. Review of the building\'s Operations and Maintenance (O&M) plan and original construction specifications, provided by the property management team, confirms that no ACM was specified or used in the construction of the buildings.
221	
222	**Lead-Based Paint (LBP).** Not applicable. All buildings on the Subject Property post-date the Consumer Product Safety Commission\'s 1978 ban on lead-based paint in residential and commercial applications.
223	
224	**Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs).** No PCB-containing transformers, capacitors, or other electrical equipment was identified on the Subject Property. Pad-mounted electrical transformers serving the buildings are labeled as containing non-PCB dielectric fluid.
225	
226	**Mold and Indoor Air Quality.** No evidence of active water intrusion, water damage, or visible mold growth was observed in any of the buildings during the site visit. A comprehensive indoor air quality assessment or mold investigation was not within the scope of this Phase I ESA.
227	
228	**Stormwater Management.** The Subject Property has an on-site stormwater management system, including two stormwater retention ponds located along the southern and western boundaries of the site. The ponds appeared to be functioning properly at the time of the site visit. Maintenance records and inspection reports for the stormwater system were provided by the property management team and appear consistent with Fairfax County maintenance requirements.
229	
230	**Southwest Corner of Building C.** The area of the Subject Property closest to the adjacent former dry cleaning parcel (Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019) was visually inspected during the site reconnaissance. No surficial staining, stressed or discolored vegetation, unusual odors, or other visual indicators of contamination were observed in this area. However, visual inspection alone is not sufficient to determine the presence or absence of subsurface contamination from migrating chlorinated solvents such as PCE, which may be present in groundwater at depths below the surface without producing visible surface indicators.
231	
232	**Interviews.** Marcus Ellison, President of Meridian GP Inc. (the general partner of the Seller), stated during an interview conducted on July 29, 2024, that he was not aware of any environmental contamination affecting the Subject Property. Mr. Ellison confirmed that he was aware of the former dry cleaning operation on the adjacent parcel and the VRP remediation conducted in 2004--2006 but stated that he had no knowledge of off-site contamination migration onto the Subject Property. Mr. Ellison further stated that no environmental testing of soil or groundwater has been conducted on the Subject Property.
233	
234	On-site property management staff, interviewed on July 30, 2024, reported no complaints from tenants in Building C or any other building regarding chemical odors, health concerns, or other issues potentially related to solvent contamination or vapor intrusion. No indoor air quality testing has been conducted in any building on the Subject Property.
235	
236	**[Section 6: Findings and Opinions]{.underline}**
237	
238	**6.1 Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs)**
239	
240	**One (1) Recognized Environmental Condition was identified in connection with the Subject Property:**
241	
242	**REC-1: Potential Tetrachloroethylene (PCE) Groundwater Migration from Adjacent Former Dry Cleaning Facility**
243	
244	A former commercial dry cleaning facility (\"Reston Village Cleaners\") operated on the parcel immediately to the southwest of the Subject Property (Fairfax County Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019) from approximately 1985 to 2003. Tetrachloroethylene (also known as perchloroethylene, or \"PCE\") was used as the primary dry cleaning solvent at the facility. Virginia DEQ Voluntary Remediation Program records (VRP File No. VRP-00487) document both soil and groundwater contamination at the former dry cleaning site. PCE was detected in groundwater at concentrations up to 87 µg/L in a monitoring well located on the southern boundary of the adjacent parcel --- a concentration significantly exceeding the Virginia Groundwater Quality Standard for PCE of 5 µg/L (an exceedance factor of approximately 17.4 times the standard).
245	
246	The VRP closure issued by Virginia DEQ in March 2006 addressed the adjacent parcel only. The closure letter explicitly noted that \"groundwater impacts associated with the former dry cleaning operation may extend beyond the boundaries of the Property\" and that \"further investigation of potential off-site migration may be warranted.\" No investigation of potential off-site migration toward the Subject Property has been conducted.
247	
248	Regional groundwater flow direction is generally from the northeast to the southwest. The Subject Property, specifically the southwest corner of the site where Building C (11640 Corporate Park Drive) is situated, is cross-gradient to slightly downgradient of the former dry cleaning facility location. This hydrogeologic positioning means that PCE-impacted groundwater could be migrating from the adjacent parcel toward and potentially beneath the Subject Property, particularly in the vicinity of Building C.
249	
250	PCE is a dense non-aqueous phase liquid (DNAPL) that, once released into the subsurface environment, can migrate vertically through soil and horizontally through groundwater over significant distances. The fractured rock and alluvial aquifer systems characteristic of the Reston, Virginia area are particularly susceptible to DNAPL migration through preferential flow pathways in bedrock fractures.
251	
252	**Based on the foregoing, Clearfield considers the potential migration of PCE-impacted groundwater from the adjacent parcel onto the Subject Property to constitute a Recognized Environmental Condition as defined by ASTM E1527-21.**
253	
254	PCE is a chlorinated volatile organic compound classified by the United States Environmental Protection Agency as a likely human carcinogen. PCE contamination plumes originating from dry cleaning facilities are well-documented in the environmental remediation literature to require extensive and costly investigation and remediation programs. Depending on the nature, extent, and severity of contamination, remediation approaches may include groundwater extraction and treatment (pump-and-treat systems), soil vapor extraction (SVE), in-situ chemical oxidation (ISCO), enhanced reductive dechlorination (ERD), or long-term monitored natural attenuation (MNA), or some combination of these technologies. Remediation costs for PCE dry cleaner contamination vary widely but commonly range from several hundred thousand dollars to in excess of \$5,000,000, and in cases involving extensive groundwater plumes, DNAPL presence at depth, or vapor intrusion concerns requiring building mitigation, costs can exceed \$10,000,000.
255	
256	**6.2 Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (CRECs)**
257	
258	No Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions were identified in connection with the Subject Property.
259	
260	**6.3 Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (HRECs)**
261	
262	No Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions were identified in connection with the Subject Property.
263	
264	**6.4 De Minimis Conditions**
265	
266	**DMC-1:** Minor quantities of typical commercial building maintenance chemicals --- including general-purpose cleaning supplies, touch-up paint, and mechanical lubricants --- were observed in properly labeled containers in designated maintenance storage areas within each building. These materials are present in quantities and conditions consistent with normal commercial building operations and are not considered to represent environmental concerns.
267	
268	**6.5 Business Environmental Risks --- Not Within ASTM E1527-21 Scope but Noted for Informational Purposes**
269	
270	**Vapor Intrusion Potential.** If PCE-impacted groundwater has migrated from the adjacent former dry cleaning parcel beneath the Subject Property, there is a potential risk of vapor intrusion into Building C and potentially into other buildings on the Subject Property. Vapor intrusion is a process by which volatile organic compounds (VOCs) present in contaminated soil or groundwater volatilize and migrate upward through the unsaturated soil zone and building foundations into indoor air, potentially resulting in exposure to building occupants at concentrations of health concern. While no tenant complaints or chemical odors were noted during the site visit, and no visual indicators of vapor intrusion were observed, vapor intrusion assessment is not within the standard scope of a Phase I ESA and would require a Phase II investigation incorporating sub-slab soil gas sampling and/or indoor air sampling to evaluate.
271	
272	This observation is provided for informational purposes as a Business Environmental Risk and is outside the scope of ASTM E1527-21 but is considered relevant to the Client\'s transaction decision-making and risk assessment.
273	
274	**[Section 7: Recommendations]{.underline}**
275	
276	**Primary Recommendation --- Phase II Environmental Site Assessment**
277	
278	Clearfield recommends that a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment be conducted prior to or as a condition of the proposed acquisition to evaluate the potential migration of PCE-impacted groundwater from the adjacent former dry cleaning facility (Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019) onto the Subject Property. The Phase II investigation should include, at a minimum, the following scope:
279	
280	> 1\. **Installation of Groundwater Monitoring Wells.** A minimum of three groundwater monitoring wells should be installed along the southwestern boundary of the Subject Property, positioned between the former dry cleaning facility site and Building C, to delineate the lateral and vertical extent of any PCE groundwater contamination plume that may have migrated onto the Subject Property.
281	>
282	> 2\. **Groundwater Sampling and Laboratory Analysis.** Groundwater samples should be collected from the newly installed monitoring wells and analyzed for volatile organic compounds (VOCs) by EPA Method 8260, with particular attention to PCE and its common degradation products, including trichloroethylene (TCE), cis-1,2-dichloroethylene (cis-1,2-DCE), and vinyl chloride.
283	>
284	> 3\. **Sub-Slab Soil Gas Sampling.** Sub-slab soil gas sampling should be conducted beneath the ground-floor slab of the southwest corner of Building C (11640 Corporate Park Drive) to evaluate the potential for vapor intrusion of PCE and related VOCs into the building interior.
285	>
286	> 4\. **Indoor Air Sampling.** Indoor air sampling should be conducted in tenant spaces on the ground floor of Building C as warranted by the results of the sub-slab soil gas sampling program.
287	
288	The Phase II investigation should be designed and executed to determine whether contamination from the adjacent former dry cleaning site has migrated onto the Subject Property and, if contamination is present, to characterize the nature and extent of such contamination with sufficient detail to support estimation of potential remediation costs and assessment of the Client\'s liability exposure.
289	
290	**Estimated Phase II Cost.** Clearfield estimates the cost of the recommended Phase II investigation at approximately \$45,000 to \$65,000, depending on encountered subsurface conditions, the number of monitoring wells ultimately required, drilling conditions, and the scope of analytical testing indicated by initial results.
291	
292	**Timing.** Clearfield recommends that the Phase II investigation be initiated promptly given the Client\'s reported due diligence timeline. Clearfield can mobilize field work within approximately 10 to 14 business days of written authorization to proceed and anticipates providing preliminary analytical results within approximately four to six weeks following completion of field activities.
293	
294	**Additional Recommendation --- Virginia DEQ Coordination**
295	
296	Clearfield recommends that a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request be submitted to the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality for the complete VRP case file (VRP File No. VRP-00487) associated with the adjacent parcel (Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019). The complete file may contain additional sampling data, remedial action reports, monitoring well logs, contaminant fate-and-transport modeling, and the Certificate of Satisfactory Completion of Remediation with any associated conditions, restrictions, or institutional controls. Clearfield has reviewed summary records available through the DEQ online database system, but the complete case file may provide additional detail regarding the documented extent and migration direction of the PCE groundwater plume.
297	
298	**Additional Recommendation --- Review of Transaction Environmental Protections**
299	
300	Given the identified Recognized Environmental Condition, Clearfield recommends that the Client and its legal counsel carefully review any environmental indemnification provisions, environmental insurance policies, escrow arrangements, or other financial protections available to the Client in connection with the proposed acquisition transaction. The potential costs of investigation and remediation of a PCE groundwater plume, if present beneath the Subject Property, could be significant, and the Client should ensure that adequate financial protections are in place to address potential environmental liabilities associated with this condition.
301	
302	**[Section 8: Limiting Conditions and Qualifications]{.underline}**
303	
304	This Executive Summary is subject to the complete limiting conditions and qualifications set forth in Section 1.7 of the full Phase I ESA report (Report No. CEC-2024-0812-MCC). The following principal limiting conditions apply:
305	
306	> 1\. This assessment was performed in accordance with the scope and limitations of ASTM E1527-21. A Phase I Environmental Site Assessment is not designed to identify all environmental conditions that may exist at a property, but only those Recognized Environmental Conditions, Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions, and Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions that are identifiable through the assessment methodology defined by the ASTM standard.
307	>
308	> 2\. No sampling, testing, or laboratory analysis of soil, groundwater, surface water, air, building materials, or other environmental media was conducted as part of this Phase I ESA. The findings and opinions expressed herein are based solely on records review, historical research, site reconnaissance, and interviews conducted in accordance with ASTM E1527-21.
309	>
310	> 3\. The findings and opinions expressed herein are based on information available to Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC as of the date of this report. Environmental conditions at the Subject Property or adjoining properties may change over time, and Clearfield assumes no obligation to update this report based on conditions arising after the date of the assessment.
311	>
312	> 4\. This report was prepared for the exclusive use of Calverley Capital Partners LLC and its authorized agents, consultants, and lenders in connection with the proposed acquisition of the Subject Property. No other party may rely upon this report without the prior written consent of Clearfield Environmental Consulting LLC.
313	>
314	> 5\. Clearfield\'s liability in connection with this report is limited to the professional fee paid for this assessment, except as may otherwise be agreed in writing between Clearfield and the Client.
315	
316	**Reliance Authorization.** In addition to the Client, this report may be relied upon by the following parties, subject to the limiting conditions stated herein and in the full Phase I ESA report:
317	
318	> • Pinnacle National Bank, as prospective lender in connection with the proposed acquisition
319	>
320	> • Hargrave, Mitchell & Stone LLP, as legal counsel to the Client
321	>
322	> • Commonwealth Title & Escrow LLC, as title and escrow agent for the proposed acquisition

325

I have performed this assessment in conformance with the standards and practices set forth in ASTM E1527-21.

S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/real-estate/extract-psa-key-terms/scenario-02/claude-code-session/20261016-023845; $S $R 'cat > /workspace/build/part6.py <<"EOF"
from lib import *

def build_env(doc):
    doc.add_heading("Part 7 — Environmental: Phase I Findings vs. PSA Protections", level=1)
    para(doc, "**Phase I key findings (Clearfield, Aug. 15, 2024; ASTM E1527-21).** One REC (REC-1): potential PCE groundwater migration from the former Reston Village Cleaners (operated ≈1985–2003) on adjacent Tax Map Parcel 0264-01-0019, southwest of the Property. DEQ VRP File VRP-00487: ≈200 cy PCE soil removed (2005); Certificate of Satisfactory Completion (March 2006) covers the adjacent parcel only; groundwater PCE up to **87 µg/L vs. 5 µg/L standard (≈17.4×)**; DEQ closure letter warns impacts “may extend beyond the boundaries” and “further investigation of potential off-site migration may be warranted.” Building C is cross-gradient to slightly downgradient; PCE is a DNAPL and local fractured-rock aquifers favor migration. No CRECs or HRECs. Business environmental risk: vapor intrusion into Building C. No soil, groundwater or indoor-air testing has ever occurred on the Property (per Seller’s Marcus Ellison). Recommended Phase II: ≥3 monitoring wells on SW boundary, VOC analysis (EPA 8260 for PCE, TCE, cis-1,2-DCE, vinyl chloride), sub-slab soil gas under Building C, indoor air as warranted; cost $45,000–$65,000; mobilization 10–14 BD after authorization; preliminary results 4–6 weeks after fieldwork. Also recommended: FOIA for full DEQ VRP file. Remediation cost range cited: several hundred thousand dollars to over $5,000,000; can exceed $10,000,000 with extensive plumes, deep DNAPL or vapor mitigation.", size=9.5)
    rows = [
        ["Magnitude of exposure", "§8.4(a) cap $3,000,000 (3.4% of price); no basket.", "Cap is below the Phase I’s upper ranges (> $5M; > $10M with vapor intrusion). Uncovered exposure could exceed the entire Deposit and Seller’s rep Cap combined."],
        ["Duration", "§8.4(b)–(c): 36 months (to Jan 15, 2028); notice must include estimated cost.", "PCE plumes are often discovered/characterized over years; DEQ processes and remediation (pump-and-treat, ISCO, ERD, MNA) frequently run longer than 3 years. Requirement to state an ‘estimated cost’ in the notice can be hard to meet early."],
        ["Trigger / causation", "Pre-Existing Environmental Conditions = conditions existing prior to the Closing Date, including migration.", "Seller may argue that post-Closing continued migration from an off-site source is not ‘attributable to conditions existing prior to Closing.’ Clarify that continued migration of a pre-Closing release (including from Parcel 0264-01-0019) is covered."],
        ["Representation", "§7.1(k): knowledge-qualified and excludes matters disclosed in the Phase I.", "REC-1 is disclosed in the Phase I, so the rep provides essentially no protection for it. Ellison confirmed awareness of the dry cleaner and the VRP; ‘knowledge’ is limited to him."],
        ["Release / as-is", "§§8.1, 8.3: as-is and broad release of environmental claims (incl. statutory) except §8.4 and Article VII.", "Buyer releases CERCLA cost-recovery/contribution and Virginia statutory claims against Seller beyond the $3M cap. Consider carving out claims for REC-1 or third-party/governmental claims."],
        ["Credit support", "None.", "Seller is a single-asset LP that will likely distribute proceeds after Closing; no escrow, holdback, parent guaranty or insurance backs the indemnity."],
        ["Pre-Closing walk right", "DD termination only through Nov 21, 2024; §9.1(d) MAC limited to changes in physical condition after the Effective Date.", "Pre-existing contamination identified after Nov 21 would not be a ‘change’ and gives no termination right — $3.5M at risk."],
        ["Diligence access", "§4.3 permits Phase I/II, business hours only, 24-hour notice; tenant interviews require consent.", "Drilling and sub-slab sampling are invasive despite ‘non-invasive’ wording; indoor-air sampling requires Building C tenant cooperation (5 tenants; includes Blue Ridge Behavioral Health PC). Obtain Seller’s written access agreement now."],
        ["CERCLA defenses", "—", "BFPP/contiguous property owner defenses require AAI components within 180 days (database 7/15/2024 lapses 1/11/2025) and post-acquisition ‘reasonable steps’ and cooperation obligations; the Phase I client is Calverley, not the PSA Buyer (Bridgewater) or the future SPE."],
    ]
    table(doc, ["Issue", "PSA Provision", "Gap / Risk"], rows, widths=[1.3, 2.2, 3.2], size=8.5, first_col_bold=True)
    para(doc, "**Assessment.** In light of REC-1, the $3,000,000 / 36-month indemnity is not adequate as drafted. Recommended package (in order of preference): (1) complete the Phase II before any money goes hard via a DD extension or environmental contingency; (2) if Phase II confirms impacts, re-price or require Seller to fund an escrow sized to a consultant’s remediation/vapor-mitigation estimate; (3) increase the §8.4 cap to at least $10,000,000 (or uncapped as to REC-1) with survival of not less than 5–10 years or until DEQ closure; (4) environmental holdback/escrow at Closing (e.g., $3–5 million) or creditworthy parent guaranty; (5) a pollution legal liability (PLL) policy with Seller cost-sharing; and (6) a release carve-out for REC-1 and third-party/governmental claims, with a cooperation covenant for claims against the adjacent owner/VRP participant.", size=9.5)

def build_concerns(doc):
    doc.add_heading("Part 8 — Responses to GC’s Specific Areas of Concern", level=1)
    doc.add_heading("8.1 Are Calverley’s deposits fully protected if financing doesn’t come through?", level=3)
    para(doc, "**No.** The deposit schedule and the financing contingency are misaligned. The scenarios are:", size=9.5)
    rows = [
        ["Terminate in DD Period (by 5:00 p.m. ET Nov 21, 2024)", "§§4.1, 4.4, 10.1", "Initial Deposit ($2.0M) refunded; Additional Deposit not yet due.", "Protected"],
        ["Title objection not cured — terminate", "§5.3", "Full Deposit refunded.", "Protected"],
        ["Financing not obtained — terminate by 5:00 p.m. ET Dec 6, 2024", "§10.2(b)", "Only the Initial Deposit ($2.0M) is refunded. The $1.5M Additional Deposit (funded Nov 29) is not addressed; under §3.4 Seller will assert retention; dispute/interpleader likely (§12.3).", "**$1.5M + interest AT RISK**"],
        ["Financing fails after Dec 6 (e.g., lender conditions such as SNDAs or Phase II unmet)", "§10.2(c)", "Contingency irrevocably waived; failure to close is a Buyer default — Seller retains $3.5M as liquidated damages (§12.1).", "**$3.5M AT RISK**"],
        ["Estoppel condition fails", "§9.3", "Full Deposit refunded (or waive / 15-day extension).", "Protected"],
        ["Material adverse rep change", "§7.2", "Full Deposit refunded.", "Protected"],
        ["Material casualty / condemnation", "§§11.1(a), 11.2(a)", "Full Deposit refunded.", "Protected"],
        ["Seller default", "§12.2", "Full Deposit + up to $500K costs, or specific performance.", "Protected"],
        ["Adverse Phase II results after Nov 21", "§§8.2, 9.1(d)", "No termination right; walking away = Buyer default.", "**$3.5M AT RISK**"],
    ]
    table(doc, ["Scenario", "PSA §", "Outcome", "Status"], rows, widths=[1.9, 0.8, 3.0, 1.0], size=8.5)
    para(doc, "**Fix:** amend §10.2(b) to return the entire Deposit; alternatively defer the Additional Deposit to 3 BD after the Financing Contingency Deadline (or make it due on the later of Nov 29 and satisfaction/waiver of the financing contingency). Also align Pinnacle’s commitment conditions (SNDAs, estoppels, Phase II, Phase I update) with PSA closing conditions.", size=9.5)
    doc.add_heading("8.2 Are the estoppel and SNDA thresholds clear and achievable?", level=3)
    para(doc, "The 80% estoppel test is reasonably clear but tight: Valerian’s estoppel is mandatory, and losing any two of the larger tenants can fail the test (Part 5). Seller’s obligation is only “commercially reasonable efforts,” the delivery deadline (Dec 31, 2024) falls in the holiday period, the form lacks lender-critical items, there is no “clean estoppel” standard, no staleness limit, no Seller-estoppel backstop, and the form names Calverley rather than the PSA Buyer. SNDAs are not a condition at all, despite Pinnacle being named in §9.4 — a gap if Pinnacle’s commitment requires them. See Flags 6–7.", size=9.5)
    doc.add_heading("8.3 Can Calverley assign to a newly formed SPE?", level=3)
    para(doc, "Yes, without Seller consent, if the SPE qualifies as an affiliate (control test measured against the PSA Buyer, Bridgewater) and the §14.3 conditions are met: executed assignment and assumption delivered ≥10 BD before Closing (Dec 31, 2024 for Jan 15), assumption of all obligations, and continuing joint and several liability of the original Buyer before and after Closing. Issues: Buyer identity (Flag 1), undefined “designee,” perpetual assignor liability, and need to confirm the SPE receives the benefit of reps, the environmental indemnity, estoppels, Phase I reliance and the title policy. See Flag 9.", size=9.5)
    doc.add_heading("8.4 Is the environmental indemnity adequate?", level=3)
    para(doc, "No — see Part 7 and Flags 3–5.", size=9.5)
EOF
echo ok'

S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/real-estate/extract-psa-key-terms/scenario-02/claude-code-session/20261016-023845; $S $R 'cat > /workspace/build/part7.py <<"EOF"
from lib import *
FLAGS = [
 ["1","Critical","Buyer entity mismatch\n§Preamble, §7.5(a), signature page, Exhs. C, D, H vs. §15.2, Exh. E, Phase I","The contracting Buyer is Bridgewater Capital Partners LLC (DE, formed 3/14/2019), signed by Kowalski and Venkataraman as Managing Members. The Buyer notice party (§15.2), the estoppel addressee/“Buyer” in Exh. E, the Phase I client/user and the instruction email all name Calverley Capital Partners LLC (the GC’s email domain is bridgewatercap.com, suggesting a rebrand or affiliate). Consequences: (i) Phase I reliance and AAI ‘user’ status may not run to the PSA Buyer; (ii) estoppels in the Exh. E form would certify to an entity that is not the Buyer; (iii) §14.3 affiliate test is measured against Bridgewater; (iv) lender loan documents and title insurance must name the correct vesting entity.","Confirm the legal relationship (name change, affiliate, or error) with organizational documents. Amend PSA to correct/confirm the Buyer (or document a §14.3 assignment); conform §15.2 and Exhs. C–E and H; obtain a Clearfield reliance letter running to the PSA Buyer, the SPE and Pinnacle."],
 ["2","Critical","Additional Deposit goes hard before financing contingency expires\n§§3.3, 3.4, 10.2(b)–(c)","Additional Deposit ($1.5M) due Nov 29, 2024; financing deadline Dec 6, 2024. §10.2(b) refunds only the Initial Deposit; §3.4 makes the termination provision control. All other termination rights refund the full Deposit, so the omission will be read as deliberate. Also, §10.2(c) waiver on Dec 6 leaves Buyer exposed to the full $3.5M if Pinnacle later declines to fund (e.g., unsatisfied SNDA/estoppel/environmental conditions). ‘Commercially reasonable and diligent efforts’ invites Seller challenge.","Amend §10.2(b) to refund the entire Deposit; or defer the Additional Deposit to 3 BD after the Financing Contingency Deadline; consider extending the deadline to align with Phase II results; obtain Pinnacle commitment with conditions mirrored in PSA §9.1."],
 ["3","Critical","Environmental indemnity inadequate for REC-1\n§§7.1(k), 8.1, 8.3, 8.4","$3.0M cap vs. Phase I range up to >$5M (>$10M with vapor intrusion); 36-month survival; notice must estimate cost; ‘attributable to conditions existing prior to Closing’ creates a continuing-migration argument; rep excludes all Phase I-disclosed matters; release waives all other environmental claims; no escrow/guaranty from single-asset Seller.","See Part 7 package: higher cap (≥$10M or uncapped for REC-1), 5–10 yr survival or until DEQ closure, escrow/holdback or guaranty, PLL insurance, clarify migration coverage, carve REC-1 out of §8.3 release, include vapor mitigation, tenant claims, lost rent and diminution in value; add Buyer control of remediation to commercial standards."],
 ["4","Critical","Phase II timeline exceeds the Due Diligence Period\n§§4.1, 4.3, 8.2","Even if authorized now (≈Oct 10–14), Clearfield mobilizes ≈Oct 25–31; field work plus 4–6 weeks for preliminary data puts results in early-to-mid December 2024 — after Nov 21 DD expiry and the Nov 29 Additional Deposit, and possibly after Dec 6. Post-DD discovery gives no termination right.","Authorize Phase II and DEQ FOIA immediately; request expedited lab turnaround. Seek a DD extension or a separate environmental contingency running to 10 BD after receipt of final Phase II results, with full Deposit refund; if Seller refuses, defer the Additional Deposit until results are in."],
 ["5","High","Phase I viability, scope and reliance\nPhase I §§1, 8; PSA §4.2(d)","Phase I components must be within 180 days of acquisition for AAI/CERCLA defenses: database (7/15/2024) lapses 1/11/2025; site visit (7/29–30) lapses 1/25/2025 — before or near Closing and certainly before an extended Closing. We have only the Executive Summary; reliance is limited to Calverley, Pinnacle, HMS and Commonwealth Title (not Bridgewater or the SPE). Clearfield’s liability is capped at its fee. §4.2(d) treats the Buyer-commissioned Phase I as a Seller deliverable, reinforcing the §7.1(k) carve-out.","Order Phase I update to be completed within 180 days before Closing (including user environmental lien/AUL search and user questionnaire); obtain the full report; add reliance for Bridgewater, the SPE and lender successors; plan post-closing BFPP ‘reasonable steps’ compliance."],
 ["6","High","SNDAs not a closing condition\n§§9.1(f), 9.4","Five tenants >15,000 RSF (Valerian, NovaTech, Chesapeake, Athena, RedPoint = 181,600 SF, 70.3% of leased SF) are targeted, but failure is excused if Seller used commercially reasonable efforts. Pinnacle will likely require SNDAs as a funding condition; the financing contingency expires Dec 6, well before SNDAs are likely to be returned. §9.1(f) (‘SNDAs required by Section 9.4’) is internally inconsistent with §9.4.","Obtain Pinnacle’s SNDA requirements and form now; send with estoppel requests; amend §9.4 to make SNDAs from the >15,000 RSF tenants a condition (with full Deposit refund), or obtain lender confirmation that SNDAs are not a funding condition; fix §9.1(f) cross-reference."],
 ["7","High","Estoppel condition — threshold, form and timing\n§9.3; Exh. E","80% of leased SF = 206,512 SF; Valerian (62,400 SF) is indispensable; slack only 51,628 SF. Seller obligation is efforts-only; deadline Dec 31, 2024 (holiday period); no ‘clean’ standard (an estoppel disclosing defaults still counts); no maximum age; no Seller estoppel backstop; Exh. E addressed to Calverley; form omits paid-through date, rent commencement/abatements, termination options (RedPoint), expansion/ROFO rights, guaranties, SNDA/subordination status, environmental/use statements, and cross-check to Exh. F. Ambiguity whether Garrison & Holt (pre-rent-commencement) ‘occupies’ space.","Amend: estoppels from (i) Valerian, NovaTech, Chesapeake, Athena and RedPoint plus (ii) 80% of leased SF in aggregate; ‘clean’ estoppels consistent with Exh. F and reps with no material adverse disclosure; dated ≤30 days before Closing; Seller estoppel backstop for up to 10% of SF; revise Exh. E (correct Buyer, add ‘affiliates, designees, successors and assigns,’ lender items); require Seller to send requests within 5 BD after Buyer approves forms."],
 ["8","High","No interim operating covenants\nArticle VII/IX (absent); §6.3","PSA contains no covenant restricting Seller, between Effective Date and Closing, from entering into, amending, renewing or terminating Leases, granting concessions, applying security deposits, entering into or modifying Service Contracts, encumbering title, removing personal property, or failing to maintain, insure and operate in the ordinary course. §6.3 refers to new leases ‘with Buyer’s prior written consent’ but imposes no consent requirement; §5.3(b) refers to encumbrances ‘in violation of this Agreement’ without an underlying covenant.","Add an interim operations covenant: ordinary-course operation, maintenance and insurance; no new/modified/terminated Leases or Service Contracts without Buyer consent (deemed approval after 5 BD during DD; sole discretion after DD); no new encumbrances; prompt notice of defaults, litigation, environmental notices; continued leasing reporting."],
 ["9","High","Assignment to SPE\n§§14.1–14.3","Permitted for ‘affiliate or designee’ but ‘designee’ is undefined and conflicts with the affiliate-only rationale of §14.2; affiliate measured against Bridgewater; notice and executed assignment ≥10 BD before Closing (Dec 31, 2024), which may precede final loan structuring; original Buyer remains jointly and severally liable for all obligations, before and after Closing, without limit in time (including §4.3, §15.8 and Exh. D/H indemnities). Lender will require SPE borrower/title vesting.","Amend §14.3: permit assignment to any entity controlled by, or under common control with, Calverley/Bridgewater or funds managed by their affiliates; reduce notice to 3 BD; release assignor at Closing from post-Closing obligations (or limit survival to pre-Closing obligations); confirm assignee benefits from reps, §8.4 indemnity, estoppels, title policy and Phase I reliance; allow collateral assignment to Pinnacle."],
 ["10","High","Dispute resolution vs. specific performance window\n§§12.2(a), 12.3, 15.4","Specific performance action must be commenced within 60 days after the scheduled Closing Date or Buyer is deemed to elect termination.
